title: The Quest for Pasupata
body:
The Quest for Pasupata

अविनाशि तु तद्विद्धि येन सर्वमिदं ततम् ।
विनाशमव्ययस्यास्य न कश्चित्कर्तुमर्हति ।।

"That which pervades the entire body, know it to be indestructible. No one can cause the destruction of the imperishable soul. (Gita II-17)"

While Yudhishthira maintained his calm, Bhima and Draupadi constantly urged him to abandon his passive stance and wage an immediate war against Hastinapur. Bhima argued that the thirteen years of exile was a calculated trap that would only allow Duryodhana to consolidate his forces. He even suggested that using certain incantations from the Atharvana Veda, they could compress thirteen years into thirteen days to fulfill their oath legally. Yudhishthira firmly rejected this, maintaining that truth (Satya) is superior to power and must be guarded at all costs.
To prepare for the inevitable war, Sage Vyasa advised Yudhishthira to send Arjuna to the Himalayas to perform austerities and acquire divine weapons from Lord Indra and Lord Shiva. Arjuna took leave of his family and ascended the rugged heights of Indrakila. There, he met Lord Indra in the guise of an old ascetic who tested his resolve by offering celestial pleasures instead of weapons. Arjuna rejected the offer, stating his sole desire was to protect Dharma on earth.
Arjuna then performed rigorous penance dedicated to Lord Shiva. One day, a wild boar charged towards Arjuna. Arjuna shot an arrow at the beast at the same instant that a local hunter (Kirata) transfixed it with a shaft. A furious dispute arose regarding who had killed the prey, culminating in a fierce combat between Arjuna and the hunter. Despite Arjuna's supreme skill, his arrows were swallowed by the hunter, and his mighty Gandiva was broken. Recognizing the hunter as none other than Lord Shiva Himself, Arjuna prostrated in total surrender. Lord Shiva, highly pleased with Arjuna's courage and humility, restored his bow and gifted him the infallible Pasupata weapon.
